title: Responsibility for payment of wages
summary: Wages must be paid on time and in full by the employer (or the person responsible under a contract of supervision, and the occupier of a factory), and a wage period cannot exceed one month.
note: Many of these provisions are now carried into the Code on Wages, 2019 - check which one applies to the establishment.

title: Time of payment of wages
summary: Wages for a wage period must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the period in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, and by the 10th day in larger establishments.
note: Late salary: this is the section to name. The Code on Wages, 2019 keeps the same rule (Sec 5).

title: Fines which may be deducted
summary: Deductions for fines are limited (in substance to the wages otherwise payable for that wage period, with a ceiling for total deductions), require a notice of the act or omission, and must be recorded in a fine register; the employee may be heard before the fine.
note: Random 'recovery', penalty for resigning, or a fine for an alleged mistake without notice is unlawful.

title: Deductions for damage or loss
summary: An employer may recover a quantifiable loss or damage caused by the employee's neglect or default, but only after giving the employee a fair opportunity to show cause, and the recovery cannot exceed the amount of the loss.
note: Ask for the show-cause notice and the quantification in writing - employers rarely have either.

title: Claims arising from deductions or delay in payment
summary: An employee (or his agent/legal heir, or a trade union/inspector acting on his behalf) may file a claim before the authority appointed by the State Government for unlawful deductions or delayed payment of wages; the authority can direct refund of the deducted amount and compensation.
note: The actual remedy route for unpaid salary and illegal deductions. Limitation for a claim is six months (verify - Sec 15(3)).

title: Offences: delaying payment of wages
summary: An employer who, without a valid reason, delays payment of wages to which an employee is entitled is punishable with fine (as notified by the State), and continued non-payment is a continuing offence.
note: Mentioning the penal section in the demand letter is standard practice; keep the tone factual.

title: Time and mode of payment of wages
summary: Wages must be paid in full and before the expiry of the wage period as notified; the Code extends the wage-based protections to all employees and removes the earlier Rs. 24,000 ceiling.
note: Not yet fully in force in all states (the four labour Codes have been repeatedly deferred) - say 'as and when notified'.

title: Individual dispute is an industrial dispute
summary: Dismissal, discharge, retention or termination of an individual workman is deemed to be an industrial dispute, so a single employee can invoke the Act even without a union.
note: Applies to 'workman' as defined (Sec 2(s)) - supervisory/managerial staff often fall outside it.

title: Continuous service
summary: A workman who has served for at least 240 days in the twelve months preceding the intended retrenchment is treated as being in continuous service, which is the gate for retrenchment protections.
note: 240 days was reduced to 180 days by the 2024 labour Codes (once notified) - check the current position.

title: Conditions precedent to retrenchment
summary: Before retrenching a workman in continuous service the employer must give one month's notice (or pay wages in lieu), pay compensation equal to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of service, and serve the notice on the appropriate Government.
note: 'Last come, first go' (Sec 25G) and the 15-days-per-year formula are the two most-litigated points.

title: Retrenchment on transfer or closure
summary: Where a undertaking is transferred, or closed, workmen are entitled to notice and compensation as if they had been retrenched.
note: Useful when an office shuts and staff are simply told to leave.

act: Industrial Establishments (Standing Orders) provisions / Shops and Establishments Acts (State)
title: Service rules, working hours, leave and notice
summary: State Shops and Establishments Acts govern working hours, weekly off, leave, holidays and notice of termination for most non-factory employees, and each state's rules must be read together with the contract of employment.
note: Always name the state: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments Act 2017, Delhi Shops and Establishments Act 2015, Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act 1961, etc.

act: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
title: Employer's and employee's contribution
summary: The employer must contribute (currently 10-12% of basic wages plus dearness and retaining allowances, as notified) and, where the employee's share is deducted from wages, must deposit it in the Fund within the prescribed time; the employee's deducted share is held in trust.
note: Deducting PF from salary and not depositing it is the classic offence - complaint to the EPFO Regional Commissioner.

act: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
title: Damages for default
summary: An employer in default of paying contributions or damages is liable to pay, in addition, damages (at a notified rate, commonly up to 10% of arrears) and prosecution can follow for continued default.
note: Verify the current damages rate - it has been revised by notification.

title: Notice and eligibility
summary: A woman who has worked in the establishment for at least eighty days in the twelve months preceding the expected date of delivery is entitled to maternity benefit; she must give notice stating that she will not work during the leave period.
note: 80 days of service is the eligibility test - not one year.

title: Twenty-six weeks of paid maternity leave
summary: Every pregnant woman is entitled to, and her employer shall not be liable for, the payment of maternity benefit at the average daily wage for the period of her actual absence - a total of twenty-six weeks, of which not more than eight weeks may be before the expected date of delivery.
note: 26 weeks was introduced by the 2017 amendment (was 12 weeks). Adopting/surrogating/commissioning mothers get twelve weeks (Sec 5(2A) area - verify).

title: Work from home after leave
summary: After the expiry of the maternity leave period, a woman may be permitted by her employer to work from home, where the nature of the work permits it, on terms mutually agreed.
note: Verify the exact subsection; the right was added by the 2017 amendment and is discretionary, not absolute.

title: No deduction of wages and discharge during maternity
summary: An employer shall not discharge or terminate a woman on account of her absence under the Act, and any such termination is unlawful; wages for the maternity period cannot be reduced.
note: The provision to quote when a woman is 'managed out' while pregnant.

title: Crèche in establishments with fifty or more employees
summary: Every establishment with fifty or more employees must provide a crèche facility, and the woman is allowed four visits a day to the crèche, which include her rest interval.
note: Added by the 2017 amendment; a common compliance failure.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Internal Committee is mandatory
summary: Every employer of a workplace with ten or more employees must constitute an Internal Committee chaired by a senior woman, with an external member from an NGO or a person familiar with the issue, and at least half the members must be women.
note: No Internal Committee = the complaint goes to the Local Committee (District Officer/District Magistrate) and the employer is penalised under Sec 26.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
title: Complaint within three months and inquiry within ninety days
summary: A written complaint may be filed within three months of the incident (extendable by three more months for sufficient cause); the inquiry must be completed within ninety days and action on the recommendations taken within sixty days.
note: Feeds the deadline tracker. Section numbers of the timelines must be re-verified.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
summary: No information of the complaint, inquiry, the names and addresses of the aggrieved woman, the respondent and witnesses, or the outcome shall be published or made available for propagation or publication, except the recommendations and the justice delivered - and identity of the woman may not be disclosed for three months after the outcome.
title: Prohibition on publication or making known of proceedings
note: This is why an employer who circulates the complaint internally is itself in breach.

title: Child marriage is voidable and an offence
summary: A marriage where either party is a child (male under 21, female under 18) is punishable and can be annulled; a petition can be filed by the child, his/her guardian, or by an organisation, and the Child Marriage Prohibition Officer is the contact at district level.
note: Insertion point for family-law queries; personal-law specifics must be verified with a lawyer.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Protection order, residence order and monetary relief
summary: An aggrieved woman in a domestic relationship can apply (free of court fee) to the Magistrate for protection, residence, monetary relief, custody and compensation orders; the right to reside in the shared household cannot be taken away by the husband or his relatives.
note: Breach of a protection order is a criminal offence (Sec 31). Verify subsection numbering.
